personal.name: Peter Kumar
personal.tagline: Cyber Security Analyst · Python Developer · AI Practitioner
personal.lede: I work where offensive security, backend engineering and AI tooling meet — probing systems for weakness, building the automation that moves data reliably at scale, and turning repetitive manual work into tools that run themselves.
personal.openTo: Cybersecurity analyst, Python developer, AI/automation and full-stack roles — including remote and contract work.

paragraphs: I'm a cyber security analyst and Python developer based in Patiala, India. My work sits where **offensive security** meets **data engineering** and **AI tooling** — probing systems for weakness, then building the tools that move data reliably at scale.

Most recently I worked as a **Cyber DevSecOps Engineer** at AWASAF Pvt. Ltd., supporting **vulnerability assessment and penetration testing** engagements and working alongside research and reporting teams to identify, document and clearly communicate security findings.

I've delivered **20+ scraping and automation projects** for business clients — extracting over **5,000 structured records** to agreed schemas and deadlines — and built production web applications in Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind, including a multi-tenant SaaS admin console running on Vercel.

I'm an active **AI practitioner**: I work daily with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity, build structured **prompt-engineering workflows**, and delegate real coding work to **agentic tools** like Codex and OpenCode.

strengths.intro: The way I work matters as much as the code I ship. These are the habits that clients and teams actually notice.

items.title: Never Lose Hope
items.text: When a task looks impossible I don't fold. I break it down, change approach and keep going until it's genuinely finished.

items.title: Never Say No to Learning
items.text: A new language, a tool I've never opened, a problem outside my comfort zone — that's an opportunity, never a reason to stop.

items.title: Eager to Learn & Catch Up
items.text: I close skill gaps on my own and fast. I don't wait for someone to teach me or hand me a roadmap.

items.title: Initiative Taker
items.text: I don't wait to be assigned. I see the problem early, tell people, and start working on it before it becomes a fire.

items.title: Strategy Builder
items.text: I turn vague goals into a clear plan — milestones, owners, deadlines and a definition of done everyone agrees on.

items.title: Self-Taught & Self-Driven
items.text: A full year of teacher-less training at NavGurukul taught me how to learn alone, stay motivated and finish what I start.

items.title: Team Leader
items.text: I've led contributors on live client projects — assigning work, unblocking people and keeping everyone shipping together.

items.title: Deadline Focused
items.text: 20+ client projects delivered against agreed dates. Reliability is the least flashy skill and the one clients remember.

items.title: Detail Obsessed
items.text: 5,000+ records validated against a client schema. In data and in security, accuracy is the entire job.

items.title: Calm Under Pressure
items.text: Live security findings, tight audit windows, client deadlines — I stay steady and keep the quality high.

items.title: Honest & Transparent
items.text: I raise concerns early and say plainly when something won't work, instead of hiding it until the deadline.

items.title: Adaptable & Versatile
items.text: Security, backend, frontend, AI, content and operations. I move between them instead of getting stuck in one lane.

blogs.intro: Longer-form write-ups where I go through a problem properly — what broke, what actually fixed it, and the reasoning behind it. Every post is a real project, and every number in it came out of a real run.

items.title: Scraping a Cloudflare-protected site without tripping the bot check
items.excerpt: Two Playwright scrapers for the same target. One gets blocked on every single run and returns nothing. The other works. They differ by four lines — and those four lines are the entire lesson.

items.title: We couldn't get leads — so we built a tool that pulls them from Google Maps
items.excerpt: Months of bought lists, scraped directories and stitched-together APIs, all failing the same way. The fix was subtraction: drop the middleware and read what Maps already publishes. 147 leads from one search, 60/60 on a clean run.

items.title: The directory, minus the noise — 2,501 Maltese businesses
items.excerpt: 8,769 public listings from a Maltese business directory, folded into 2,501 businesses. Four columns — name, phone, email, website — with the gaps left visible instead of quietly filled in.

promptEngineering.title: Prompt Engineering
promptEngineering.claim: I'm good at it — and I treat it as engineering, not guessing.
items: Write precise, role-scoped prompts with explicit context, constraints and a defined output format
Chain prompts into repeatable workflows instead of one-off questions
Force structured output — JSON, tables, checklists — that pipes straight into code
Iterate and self-critique to strip vague or hallucinated answers out
Build domain-tuned prompt sets for scraping rules, pentest checklists and client reports
Document and version my prompt templates so others on the team reuse them too

recommendations.name: Anum Yusuf
recommendations.text: Peter delivered a web scraping, SQL, and machine learning project on time and fully to specification. He showed excellent technical depth in scraping — efficient extraction and processing across multiple sources — and built the SQL data layer in a clean, well-structured way that showed real command of data handling and query optimization. The machine learning component was particularly strong: well-chosen models, rigorous evaluation, and results presented with clear analysis. The work was consistently of high quality, reflecting dedication and close attention to detail, and I am very satisfied with the outcome.

recommendations.name: Manoj Pokhrael
recommendations.text: I have been consistently impressed by the way Peter runs a project. Communication is genuinely open — he listens closely to what is actually being asked and raises concerns clearly and early, which keeps everything on track. Meeting deadlines has been a real strength, and his availability for discussion makes the whole process run smoothly. It has been a pleasure working together, and I look forward to our continued collaboration.

recommendations.name: Vishal Kapil
recommendations.text: Peter has been assisting me with content and social media-related work for my page, particularly with content planning, preparation, research, and keeping up with relevant current events and trends. I have found him to be sincere, dependable, proactive, and easy to work with. He understands instructions well, contributes useful ideas, and is always willing to put in the effort to get the work done properly. I would be happy to recommend him to anyone looking for a responsible and capable person for content or social media-related work.
